simple.meaning: הֵיכָל (hêykâl) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “a large public building, such as a palace or temple.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 80 times across 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, 1 Kings, 2 Kings, 2 Chronicles, and 18 more, beginning at 1 Samuel 1:9. Its contexts include kingship, priesthood.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to הֵיכָל (H1964).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: הֵיכָל (hêykâl) / H1964 is traced through 1 Samuel 1:9, 1 Samuel 3:3, 2 Samuel 22:7, 1 Kings 6:3 as a generated source-based concept entry.

definitions.short: a large public building, such as a palace or temple
